nodes.name: SSF substrate cleaning
nodes.procedure: To eliminate surface oxides and contamination, SSF substrate was subjected to cleaning with a 1 M HCl solution for 10 min to effectively eliminate the native oxide layer. Afterward, it was washed repeatedly with water and acetone under sonication to eliminate any residual impurities. Finally, it was stored in acetone to preserve its cleanliness for subsequent electrodeposition.
nodes.source_text: SSF substrate was subjected to cleaning with a 1 M HCl solution for 10 min... Finally, it was stored in acetone

nodes.name: CoP@SSF electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Electrodeposition was carried out on a three-electrode system. The working electrode, reference electrode, and counter electrode were the treated SSF electrode, Silver/Silver Chloride (Ag/AgCl), and Pt wire, respectively. The deposition bath was a mixture of 0.1 M CoCl₂·6H₂O, 0.1 M NaH₂PO₂·H₂O, and 0.12 M NH₄Cl in the deionized water. Subsequently, galvanostatic electrodeposition was performed under a current density of -40 mA cm⁻² for 4 min. Upon completing the deposition process, the CoP@SSF electrode was meticulously rinsed with deionized water to ensure the removal of any unbound species. It was then left to dry naturally at ambient temperature, rendering it ready for further surface modifications and electrochemical performance evaluations in an alkaline medium.

nodes.name: Co@SSF control electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: A reference Co deposited on SSF (Co@SSF) was prepared as a control electrode without the inclusion of NaH₂PO₂·H₂O in the deposition solution. The amount of Co (4.4 ± 0.11 mg cm⁻²) electrodeposited on the SSF substrate was determined by weighing the SSF substrate before and after the deposition process.

nodes.characterization_summary: CoP@SSF shows porous structure formed by closely packed spherical nanoparticles with absence of crystal lattice fringes and no characteristic diffraction rings in SAED pattern, confirming amorphous nature.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Higher-resolution TEM images (Fig. 1n and o) reveal the absence of crystal lattice fringes, while the selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern (Fig. 1p) lacks the characteristic diffraction rings of crystalline materials.

nodes.characterization_summary: CoP@SSF shows uniform distribution of Co and P elements across the electrode surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM-EDX elemental mapping analysis of CoP@SSF (Fig. 1i-l) reveals a uniform distribution of the key elements, Co and P, across the electrode surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: CoP@SSF is predominantly amorphous - no CoP diffraction peaks at 2θ=48.13° (expected strongest reflection), only SSF substrate peaks visible. Co@SSF shows hexagonal Co peaks at 2θ=41.14°(100), 44.34°(002), 46.92°(101).
nodes.evidence_snippet: No CoP diffraction peaks are observed at 2θ = 48.13° (see inset of Fig. 2a), where no overlap with the SSF substrate occurs and cobalt phosphide is expected to exhibit its strongest reflection (PDF#29–0497).

nodes.characterization_summary: CoP@SSF: Co 2p3/2 at 774.94 eV (Co-P, +0.76 eV shift vs metallic Co), 781.13 eV (Co²⁺); P 2p at 128.1 eV (Co-P, -0.4 eV vs elemental P), 133.69 eV (P-O phosphates). Co@SSF: Co 2p3/2 at 774.18 eV (Co⁰), 780.68 eV (Co²⁺).
nodes.evidence_snippet: For CoP@SSF, the Co 2p spectrum shows a peak at 774.94 eV, assigned to cobalt phosphide (Co–P)... This peak is positively shifted by ∼0.76 eV relative to metallic cobalt... The high-resolution spectrum of P 2p exhibits a weak peak at 128.1 eV, corresponding to P–Co bonds.

nodes.characterization_summary: No detectable cobalt leached into electrolyte after 130 h HER/OER testing of CoP@SSF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After 130 h of HER testing, we used AAS to determine the amount of cobalt leached into the electrolyte. The cobalt level was below the detection limit.
